findings.text: RLSECURITY-1: test-author answered not mine: the code must change: `plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh`: when `_ccgl_race_note_post_v` returns rc 2 (note posted but no numeric id returned), `note_id` remains empty; `_ccgl_race_note_update` returns early because `[[ "$id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]` fails, so DSRACE-3's requirement is silently not met. A test asserting DSRACE-3 holds for rc-2 would fail on the current new code — it cannot "pass once the code is written" unless the code also changes. — the finding: security lens, medium: When `_ccgl_race_note_post_v` returns rc 2 (POST succeeded but GitHub's reply carried no numeric id), `note_id` remains empty; in the loser path `_ccgl_race_note_update` immediately returns 0 because `[[ "$id" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]` fails, so DSRACE-3's requirement (the loser PATCHes its note body to "not started — concurrent claim: `<winner>` was first") is silently not met. (plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh: "_ccgl_race_note_post_v note_id "$_CCGL_SLUG" "$issue" "$my_holder" || note_rc=$?"; happens when: GitHub's comment-create response arrives without an "id" field (malformed reply, rate-limit truncation, or a future API change) while two runs claim at once; the note exists on GitHub and participates in arbitration, but the loser leaves it unupdated, violating DSRACE-3.; fix: test; ACCEPTED IF: when the note was posted (rc 0 or rc 2 from _ccgl_race_note_post_v) but no numeric id is known and the run loses the race, DSRACE-3 is either satisfied by an alternative update path, or the design explicitly accepts the gap and the test for DSRACE-3 covers the rc-2 case.); the same kind of problem also at: plugins/claim-coordinator/github-labels/plugin.sh | _ccgl_race_note_delete "$note_id" "$_CCGL_SLUG" "$issue"
